lines.text: All labor and success spring from a man's envy of his neighbor, and one handful with tranquility is better.
A man all alone, without a wife or brother, has eyes still not content with his wealth.
Two are better than one because of their good return, and a companion can lift up one who falls.
If two lie down together they keep warm, and a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
A poor wise youth is better than an old foolish king and came from the palace to kingship.
